trajectory_summary: The call opens neutral, briefly cracks open when the customer says he's 'more willing to listen' despite his skepticism, then collapses when the rep validates his low-bill objection and disqualifies him over the tree rather than exploring it further. Energy leaked at the exact moment it could have been captured.
outcome_dispute: This should not be read as a clean roof/shade DQ — the rep manufactured the disqualification by agreeing with the customer's own low-bill/no-shade-tolerance framing rather than testing whether the design team could work around one back tree.

observed_outcome.quote:
So,
yeah, like you said, you're not open to removing the trees at all, so solar won't work for you. I can just remove you from my list.
observed_outcome.reasoning: Rep explicitly ends pursuit citing the shade/tree issue as the disqualifying gate, and the call terminates with no next step.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: Bill was captured ('is around 76 to $81') but the rep never flipped it into a reason to proceed — instead the rep agreed at 01:57 'Your bill isn't extremely high,' which is the line where the flip should have gone.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep did not request the actual utility bill or a photo/email during the call.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep did not ask what motivated the customer to look into solar; the customer discussed payback concerns but did not state a reason for interest in solar.
